title: Ironhollow Rising Revisited
premise: In the city of Ironhollow, where the gods were bound and magic outlawed twelve years ago, Petra Okonkwo has survived by carving bone charms too small to notice—until the old gods stir and her charms begin to answer prayers. Drawn into the rebellion of a disgraced priest, Tam, whose love she cannot afford, Petra learns the king is not a man but a hollow vessel wearing the crown of the god of endings, sustained by the souls of the bound dead—including, she discovers, her mother. To free the king and the city, Petra must unbind the god at the cost of her own gift, her mother's last remnant, and nearly her life. In the end, the king dies human and the gods scatter free, and Petra, deaf to the dead for the first time, chooses to stay in Ironhollow with Tam and rebuild among the living.
about_author: Jude Sterling is the pen name of a former museum conservator who spent a decade restoring funerary art before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about grief, craft, and the stubborn persistence of the living.

chapters.title: Small Charms
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. In the market of Ironhollow, Petra sells a bone charm to a grieving mother—and hears, for the first time in years, the dead whisper back through it. She destroys the charm in terror. Beat: the safe invisibility she built is cracking.

chapters.title: The Law of Quiet
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Wardens raid the carver's quarter; her neighbor is taken for a charm that worked. Petra realizes her carvings are waking, not hers alone—the old gods are answering. Beat: fear curdling into guilt for those her silence failed.

chapters.title: A Priest in the Gutter
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam, a priest of the bound gods hiding as a lamplighter, traces the working charms to Petra's stall and begs her help. She refuses. Beat: the ache of recognition—two people who remember the same lost world.

chapters.title: What the Bones Say
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. A dead child's voice leads Petra to a mass grave from the Binding, where she hears her mother's soul among the bound. She seeks out Tam. Beat: grief weaponized into resolve.

chapters.title: The Hollow King
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. At a state procession, Tam watches King Aldric and sees the wrongness: no soul behind the eyes, the crown drinking from him. He understands the Binding never ended—it just moved into the palace. Beat: dread.

chapters.title: Terms of the Living
chapters.summary: Petra and Tam, dual POV. In a smuggler's cellar, they bargain: Petra will unbind the dead if Tam's underground will shelter her. Their first kiss is interrupted by a warden's whistle. Beat: love offered against duty, deferred.

chapters.title: The Warden's Mercy
chapters.summary: Warden Ilsa's POV. Ilsa, who took Petra's neighbor, interrogates a captured rebel and begins to doubt the law she enforces. She lets a child go—and files a false report. Beat: complicity and conscience.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Flashback to the night of the Binding: how Petra survived by carving her mother's soul into a charm and hiding it, and how the guilt of that survival has shaped every year since. Beat: the price of survival made explicit.

chapters.title: The God of Endings
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. In the sealed temple, Tam performs the old rites and makes contact with the bound god of endings, who speaks through the king's mouth: the god is not imprisoned willingly—it is being eaten. Beat: the enemy reframed as victim.

chapters.title: Charm Against Charm
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra's charms are now openly working; pilgrims crowd her stall. The wardens mark her. Ilsa warns her instead of arresting her—an uneasy alliance begins. Beat: visibility as both power and death sentence.

chapters.title: The Crown's Appetite
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Inside the palace, Ilsa sees the king feed: a courtier withers to dust at the crown's touch. She brings proof to Petra and Tam. Beat: the enemy revealed, the stakes made flesh.

chapters.title: Mother's Bone
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra's mother's soul, worn smooth by twelve years in a charm, begs her not to unbind the god—freedom for the dead means her final dissolution. Petra must choose between her mother's last wish and the city. Beat: love against duty, intimate scale.

chapters.title: The Rebel's Bargain
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam's underground splinters; half want to assassinate the king rather than free the god. Tam takes leadership by promising the impossible. Beat: duty hardening into isolation.

chapters.title: Ash Market
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Wardens burn the carver's quarter; Petra's shop and her mother's charm survive only because Ilsa smuggles them out. The neighbor's daughter is killed in the fire. Beat: rage; the cost of staying invisible too long.

chapters.title: What Ilsa Owes
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Ilsa is exposed as a sympathizer and flees to the rebels, bringing the palace's ritual calendar: the king renews the Binding at the solstice, in six days. Beat: the clock starts.

chapters.title: Six Days
chapters.summary: Petra, Tam, and Ilsa plan the unbinding: Petra must reach the crown at the solstice rite and carve the god free while Tam holds the wards open and Ilsa opens the gates. Beat: resolve forged in exhaustion.

chapters.title: The Night Before
chapters.summary: Petra and Tam's POV. On the eve of the solstice, Petra and Tam finally speak their love plainly, knowing one of them may not survive. Her mother's soul gives Petra her blessing. Beat: tenderness before ruin.

chapters.title: The Solstice Rite
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. In the throne room, Petra carves the unbinding as the crown fights back, flooding her with every bound soul at once. Tam's wards begin to fail. Beat: climax begins—overwhelm, sacrifice.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam burns his own priesthood's remaining power to hold the wards, and the god of endings, freed, must choose: devour the king's vessel or release him. Petra offers her own gift as the price. Beat: climax turns.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The god accepts: the king dies human and at peace, the dead scatter free—her mother among them, whispering goodbye—and Petra's hearing dies with them. She wakes deaf to the dead, in Tam's arms. Beat: grief and relief intertwined.

chapters.title: A City of the Living
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Weeks later: Ilsa helps rebuild the wardens into something worth trusting; the gods, freed, are distant and quiet, answering no one. Beat: the world changed, imperfectly, for the better.

chapters.title: Ironhollow Rising
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra carves again—plain bone, no magic—and hangs her mother's empty charm above the door. Tam lights the temple lamps again. For the first time, silence is not exile but peace. Beat: resolution; survival finally worth its price.
